Definition: an angle; by implication, a pinnacle; figuratively, a chieftain
BiblicalUsage: Pinnah is a corner — of a building, a wall, a field, or a people. The stone the builders refused became the head stone of the corner in Psalms 118:22, and God lays a precious corner stone in Zion in Isaiah 28:16. Zechariah 10:4 says the corner comes out of Judah, and Job 38:6 asks who laid the corner stone of the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the corner stone is Christ Himself — the stone men refused, the stone God chose to hold the whole building. That is why I hold that everything true in my life has to line up to Him.
